You are making ONE surgical fix in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, or open a PR. Do NOT send anything externally. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth engines only, zero API spend. Use PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp for every python invocation. Files you may change: server/pipeline/angle_render.py and tests/test_angle_render.py. Nothing else. Do not touch scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh (another worker owns it right now).

WHAT IS BROKEN: episode 2026-06-10-fred-cho cannot finish because the angle_segments media gate refuses segment 23. The orchestrator's gate (server/pipeline/orchestrator.py ~2637-2670) renders EVERY planned angle segment individually -- render_angle_switch([one_segment], ..., crossfade_s=0.0) -- so the failing unit is a ~2.5 second single-segment program. render_angle_switch refuses it at server/pipeline/angle_render.py ~941-960 with: 'program AUDIO disagrees with the map (audio=2.453000 map_total=2.500000)'.

WHAT A MEASURED DIAGNOSTIC RUN PROVED (2026-07-24, real renders off Fred's composite, receipts in /home/ankit114/ringer-work/podcast-full-auto-seg23/seg23-audio-vs-map-rootcause/):
  * The refusal compares the boundary map against `_stream_duration(out_path, 'a:0')` (angle_render.py ~103-119), which reads the MP4 container's stream=duration PRESENTATION field, not the decoded audio.
  * A 120s single-segment render reports stream=duration = 119.994 s while decoding to EXACTLY 5,760,000 samples at 48 kHz = 120.000000 s. The field lies; the audio is complete. (Independently re-verified by the coordinator on the same file.)
  * 2.5s and 5.0s single-segment renders decode to 120,832 and 240,640 samples -- the requested population plus 832 and 640 samples of AAC-LC terminal padding (frames are 1024 samples, so the excess is bounded by 1023).
  * The quantity is trustworthy in the other direction too: a 3-segment contiguous 10s control whose one-pass filter output is exactly 480,000 PCM samples decodes to 477,184 samples after the mux -- a REAL 2,816-sample (58.7 ms) deficit that any correct certification must still refuse.
  * ffprobe 7.1.5 on this host does NOT support -count_samples / stream=nb_read_samples. The supported equivalent is summing decoded frame nb_samples.

THE FIX (smallest change, in render_angle_switch's certification block at angle_render.py ~941-975):
1. Add a helper named EXACTLY `_count_decoded_audio_samples(path, stream="a:0")` that runs:
   ffprobe -v quiet -select_streams a:0 -show_frames -show_entries frame=nb_samples -of default=noprint_wrappers=1:nokey=1 <path>
   sums every non-empty line as an int, and returns None on ANY failure (non-zero rc, timeout, OSError, non-integer output, zero frames). Give it a generous timeout: it must not decode-blow on a 31-minute program (frame listing is cheap, but pick a timeout that survives full length, and treat a timeout as None).
2. Replace the container-duration comparison with sample certification: expected_samples = round(map_total * 48000); accept ONLY when 0 <= decoded_samples - expected_samples <= 1023. A None sample count fails the render (fail-closed, keep the existing 'refusing the render' log style and say WHY, printing decoded, expected and the delta in samples AND milliseconds).
3. Keep the existing final video frame-count check (angle_render.py ~961-975) exactly as it is -- it is what catches the historical 40-dropped-frame defect.
4. Update the block's comments to state the new arithmetic and why the container field was wrong, so the next reader does not reintroduce it.

NON-NEGOTIABLE: this must NOT become a tolerance widening. The asymmetric bound is zero samples short, at most 1023 samples long, because AAC-LC pads only the final frame. Verify in your own words in the code comment that: a 47 ms deficit (-2,256 samples), the measured multi-segment defect (-2,816 samples) and the historical mid-episode accumulation (-366 ms = -17,568 samples) ALL still fail. If your change would let any of those through, it is wrong. Never skip certification for short programs, and never certify when the probe is unavailable.

ADD TO tests/test_angle_render.py two tests named exactly:
  * test_render_audio_sample_certification_accepts_aac_padding -- proves an output carrying the expected population plus terminal AAC padding is accepted, INCLUDING the case where stream=duration disagrees with the map (the 120s/119.994s case). Prefer driving the real certification path with small synthetic media or a targeted monkeypatch of the sample-count/frame-count probes; do not assert on a hand-rolled copy of the arithmetic.
  * test_render_audio_sample_certification_rejects_real_shortfall -- proves -2,256, -2,816 and -17,568 sample deficits are each refused (render returns None), and that an unprobeable sample count is also refused.
Keep the existing tests in that file green -- especially the frame-count/single-truth and probe-failure tests.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH and paste the real output into your final message:
  cd /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp python3 -m pytest tests/test_angle_render.py -q -p no:cacheprovider
and a REAL end-to-end render proving the gate shape now passes, e.g. a scratch script that calls render_angle_switch([{'start':700.0,'end':702.5,'angle':'sbs'}], composite, composite, composite, {}, '<scratch>/gate.mp4', crossfade_s=0.0, target_size=(640,360)) against /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast/episodes/2026-06-10-fred-cho/processed/composite.mp4 and prints the returned path plus the decoded sample count. Put that scratch script in YOUR task directory, never in the repo, and never write renders into the episode directory. A claim without executed output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty -- the coordinator lands it.
tasks.verified: A real 2.5s single-segment render (the exact shape the angle_segments gate uses) now returns a path instead of being refused, its decoded audio sample count sits inside the AAC-padding-only invariant, a genuinely short multi-segment program is still never returned, and the repo's angle-render tests including the two new certification tests pass
